name: Body, Color, and Emotion 220
description: A focused list of human body parts, colors, and emotion concepts.
attribution: List, Johann Mattis & Tjuka, Annika & Blum, Frederic & Kučerová, Alžběta & Ugarte, Carlos Barrientos & Rzymski, Christoph & Greenhill, Simon & Forkel, Robert (eds.) 2025. Concepticon v3.4.0. A Resource for the Linking of Concept Lists. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. https://concepticon.clld.org

concepts.definition: Having a colour between black and white, like ash or stone.
Having red as its colour.
Dark and colourless; not reflecting visible light.
Having the pure color of a clear sky; the primary color between green and violet in the visible spectrum, an effect of light with a wavelength between 450 and 500 nm.
Bright and colourless; reflecting equal quantities of all frequencies of visible light.
Having the colour of a yolk, a lemon or gold.

Having green as its colour; having the hue of that portion of the visible spectrum lying between yellow and blue, evoked in the human observer by radiant energy with wavelengths of approximately 490 to 570 nanometers.
Having a brown color.
Having purple as its color.
Having a red to yellow metallic color that resembles the metal copper.
A bright reddish-yellowish colour.
Having pink as its colour.
A lighter variant of the color blue, mixed with white or light gray, with a wavelength between 450 and 490 nm.
A lighter variant of the color green, mixed with white or light gray, with a wavelength between 520 and 570 nm.
A darker variant of the primary color yellow, mixed with black, orange or red.
A kind of yellowish color, mixed with gray.
A yellowish-brown color which is often associated with military uniforms.
A very intense variant of the color yellow.
A light variant of the color purple which resembles the color of the flowers of a Syringa tree.
A variant of the color red but deeper and mixed with purple.
A darker variant of the color green, mixed with black, with an approximate wavelength between 543 and 549 nm.
Having a light greenish blue as its color.
A feeling of discontent or covetousness with regard to another's advantages, success, possessions, etc.
Belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins).
An emotion experienced in anticipation of some specific pain or danger.

An unpleasant complex combination of emotions that includes fear, apprehension and worry, and is often accompanied by physical sensations such as palpitations, nausea, chest pain and/or shortness of breath.
Deep awareness of the suffering of another, coupled with the wish to relieve it.
Mental suffering or pain caused by injury, loss, or despair.
The consciousness or awareness of dishonor, disgrace, or condemnation.
An unpleasant, usually localised physical sensation that is often the result of an injury, disease or other ailment.
An attitude of admiration or esteem.
A jealous feeling, disposition, state, or mood.
The feeling that one gets when seeing something rotten.
Mental happiness.
The state of being poor or emotionally suffering.
In philosophy, happiness translates the Greek concept of eudaimonia, and refers to the good life, or flourishing, rather than simply an emotion.
The strong desire for something.
A state or quality of mind that enables to face danger and fear; bravery.
The belief in the possibility that something one wants will happen.
The quality of being caring, generous and helpful towards other people.
The feeling of great sadness because someone has died.
A strong feeling of dislike for something or somebody.
A feeling of ultimate disgust and a complete lack of respect towards somebody.
A feeling of sadness because something did not happen the way it was expected or did not happen at all.
A feeling of extreme but short-term happiness.
A desire to learn about something or somebody.
A feeling caused by something unexpected.
A feeling of extreme pleasure and excitement as a result of success or a victory.
A feeling caused by doing or watching something entertaining or funny.
A feeling of deep respect mixed with slight fear or wonder.
A feeling of uncertainty about what to do or what is happening.
A feeling of being unhappy because something is missing or wrong.
A state of feeling sad that can become a chronic illness.
An emotional state of being proud.
An emotional state of sensual gratification or frivolous amusement.
A feeling of affection and fondness for someone.
A lump at the front of the neck.
Facial hair of humans on the chin, cheeks and jaw.
The fleshy organ on the chest of a sexually mature human female containing mammary glands.
The fleshy part of the human body that one sits on.
The fleshy backside of the lower part of the leg.
The lower fleshy part of the human ear.
The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.
The hard, flat, translucent covering near the tip of a human finger, useful for scratching and fine manipulation.
The part of a human’s body below the ankle that is used in order to stand and walk.
The hair on humans, usually on the head but also including the hair on the body.
The terminal hair that develops on the human body during and after puberty.
The hair on the head of humans (rather than the hair in general or the hair on the body).
The part of the human foot on the backside where it becomes the leg.
The arched part of the human foot between the ankle and the toes.
In man, the joint in the middle part of the leg.
The front area from waist to knees, especially when sitting.
The left hand of a human.
The smallest of the five fingers.
The third and longest finger on the human hand.
A growth of facial hair between the nose and the upper lip.
The inner and somewhat concave part of the human hand that extends from the wrist to the bases of the fingers.
Dense, coarse hair that grows on the male and female genital area beginning in puberty.
The right hand of a human.
The outer tissue of human beings.
The hard keratin substance covering the tips of the feet of human beings.
The central part of the human body, from which neck and limbs extend.
The external parts of the female genitalia, in human beings this consists of the labia, clitoris, opening of the urethra (meatus), and the opening of the vagina.
In human beings, the part between the thorax and hips.
A joint formed where the foot and the leg meet.
The lower opening of the digestive tract, through which faeces pass.
The upper limb, extending from the shoulder to the wrist and sometimes including the hand.
The hollow under the upper part of the arm at the shoulder.
A blood vessel transporting blood away from the heart.
The rear of body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and belly.
The back part of the head.
The lower part of the front of the torso (or a comparable part of an animal), confined by the upper side by the midriff and the lowerside by the pelvis. Contains the intestines.
A hollow muscular balloon-shaped organ that stores urine until it is excreted from the body.
The blood vessels are the part of the circulatory system that transports blood throughout the human body or an animal body.
The physical structure of a human or animal.
Part of a human body or an animal body.
Any of the components of an endoskeleton, consisting mainly of calcium phosphate, collagen and cells.
The organ of the central nervous system of an animal or human located in the skull that controls the actions and thoughts of the animal or human.
Long flat bone located in the center of the chest.
The soft skin on each side of the face, between the eyes and the chin; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
The portion of the body from the base of the neck to the top of the abdomen; the thorax.
The bottom of the face, below the mouth.
A part of the female genitalia located at the front of the vulva, consisting of a sensitive erectile body.
Bone linking the scapula and sternum.
The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea.
The joint between arm and forearm.
The organ that is sensitive to light, which it converts to electrical signals passed to the brain, by which means animals and humans see.
The partly visible orb nesting in the eye socket which contains for example pupil, retina and iris and is connected to the brain via the optic nerve.
One of the hairs that grows on the eyelid, around the eyes.
A skin flap that can be closed over an eye.
The front part of the head, featuring the eyes, nose, and mouth and the surrounding area.
One of the long extremities of the hand that is used for gripping objects.
The top of the finger.
The soft substance in the body of living things.
The finger between thumb and long finger.
The part of the face between the hairline and the eyebrows.
Aeveral teeth located above and below in the mouth of mammals (including humans) to bite food off.
A pear-shaped organ located beneath the liver that serves as a storage sac for bile until it is released into the small intestine.
The sexual organs: the testicles and penis of a male; or the labia, clitoris, and vagina of a female.
The mucosal tissue that partly lies over the teeth in the mouth.
The internal organs of an animal or human.
That part of the fore limb below the forearm or wrist in primates (including humans).
The part of the body of an animal or human which contains the brain, mouth and main sense organs.
A muscular organ that pumps blood through the body.
The outward-projecting parts of the pelvis and top of the femur and the overlying tissue.
Large, flat bone in the center.
A hump may refer to a camel's hump containing its fat reservoir or alternatively to the curve on an upper spine that causes a hunchback.
The alimentary canal of an animal or human through which food passes after having passed all stomachs.
Either of the two opposable structures forming, or near the entrance to, the mouth.
Any part of the body where two bones join.
An organ in the body that produces urine.
Joints of the fingers brought to prominence when hand is clenched.
Organ on the upper end of the trachea.
The limb of an animal (including humans) that extends from the groin to the ankle.
Either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth.
A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. Responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
The part of the body (of humans and quadrupeds) each side of the backbone between the ribs and hips.
Hair that is not cut.
The part of the arm between the elbow and the hand.
The lower part of the spine, also known as the lumbar region, which is situated between the rib cage and the pelvis.
Part of the leg between the knee and the foot.
A biological organ that extracts oxygen from the air.
A tooth located in the back of the mouth used for crushing and grinding food.
Opening in the lower half of a human face which is used for food ingestion and articulation.
An organ formed by contractile tissue that moves other organs.
The back part of the neck.
A scar where the umbilical cord was attached.
The part of the body (found in some animals, including humans) that connects the head and the trunk.
An enclosed, cable-like bundle of axons (nerve fibers, the long and slender projections of neurons) in the peripheral nervous system.
The projection of a mammary gland from which, on female mammals, milk can be secreted.
The organ of the face used to breath and smell.
Either of the two orifices located on the nose (or on the beak of a bird); used as a passage for air and other gases to travel the nasal passages.
Cavity that is limited by the lips in front, the cheeks on the side, the soft and hard palate at the top and the floor of the mouth below.
The female sex organ which is often paired and produces eggs for procreation.
The palate is the roof of the mouth in humans and other mammals.
An organ of the digestive system of vertebrates.
The male sexual organ for copulation and urination; the tubular portion of the male genitalia (excluding the scrotum).
The inner part of the neck which starts after the oral and nasal cavity.
A vascular organ that is formed inside the womb to ensure the transfer of vital nutrients and regulation of metabolic exchange between mother and the foetus.
Contractile aperture in iris.
One of the long curved bones which form the rib cage.
Anatomical male reproductive structure.
The front part of the leg below the knee.
One side of the top of the torso, where an arm attaches or joins.
A large flat bone located at the back of each shoulder.
The side of the body.
The body part that forms the supporting structure inside of the human body or the body of animals.

The tissue forming the outer covering of the vertebrate body: it consists of two layers, the outermost of which may be covered with hair, scales, feathers, etc. It is mainly protective and sensory in function.
The main bone of the head; the cranium.
The bottom of the foot.
The body part that consists of a row of vertebrae, that support the head and torso and that forms a canal for nerves.
A ductless vascular gland, located in the left upper abdomen near the stomach.
An organ in the body, involved in digestion of food.
The region of the skull on either side of the forehead.
Tissue that connects muscle to bone.
The male sex gland that produces sperm and male hormones, found in some types of animals and humans.
The front part of the neck.
The shortest and thickest of the fingers that can be placed against the others in order to create a firm grip.
The front part of the tongue.
One of the extremities of the foot.

The flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used to move food around, for tasting and that is moved into various positions to modify the flow of air from the lungs in order to produce different sounds.
A hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals (including humans), generally used for eating.
A conduit between the developing embryo or fetus and the placenta.
The part of the arm between the shoulder and the elbow.
The upper part of the back.
The part of the leg between the pelvis and the knee.
A conic projection from the posterior edge of the middle of the soft palate.
The lower part of the female reproductive tract; a moist canal in female mammals (including humans) extending from the labia minora to the uterus.
A blood vessel that transports blood from the capillaries back to the heart.
The major female reproductive organ of most mammals, including humans. It is a large muscle enveloping the phoetus during pregnancy.
The flexible and narrower connection between the forearm and the hand.
The outer opening of the ear.
A bit sad.
Having a feeling of satisfaction, enjoyment or well-being, often arising from a positive situation or set of circumstances.
To dislike intensely; to feel strong hostility towards.
To want something to happen or the belief in the possibility that something one wants will happen.
To have an intense feeling of affection and care towards another person.
Feeling greatly pleased, or satisfied by something or someone that is highly honorable or creditable to oneself.
To wish that a past event had not happened.
Feeling mentally uncomfortable because something is missing or wrong.
Feeling that something unexpected has happened.
To be anxious about something.
Full of cheerfulness and joy, often associated with festivities and celebration.
To want to do something, to wish for something to happen, or to have affection for someone.
Having desired or positive qualities.
To enjoy, be in favor/favour of.
Not good; unfavorable; negative.
To want to do something or to wish for something to happen.
Irritated, in a temper, feeling or displaying anger.
To hold somebody responsible for something.
Being nice and giving off the impression of benevolence.
Uncertainty about the truth or accuracy of a matter.
Having a feeling of security or protection from harm.
Feeling shame or guilt.
Becoming irritable in difficult situations or during long waiting times.
Feeling that something unexpected has happened.
Feeling insecure over an anticipated loss of status or affection in a human connection.
Property of being scared of something or someone, having an uncontrollable emotion of anxiety.
Enduring difficult situations or a long waiting time with an even temper.
To express deep sorrow for.
